## Joining data frames

Assume we have two data frames, `df1` and `df2`. There are some shared variable(s) across the two.

We want to combine `df1` and `df2` into one single data frame. The `dplyr` code will look something like:

::: fragment
```{r eval = F}
xxx_join(df1, df2)
```
:::

-   How do we combine `df1` and `df2` them? The following mutating joins give us rules:

    -   `left_join()`: keep all cases from `df1`
    -   `right_join()`: keep all cases from `df2`
    -   `full_join()`: keep all cases from both `df1` and `df2`
    -   `inner_join()`: keep all cases from `df1` where there are matching values in `df2` (more complicated in the scenario of multiple matches)

::: fragment
I know this is confusing! Examples will help clarify!
:::

<!-- -   Filtering joins (we won't use, but they can be helpful): -->

<!--     -   `semi_join()`: return all rows from `x` where there are matching values in `y`, keeping just columns from `x` -->

<!--     -   `anti_join()`: return all rows from `x` where there are not matching values in `y`, never duplicate rows of `x` -->

## `left_join(df1, df2)`

Adds columns to `df1` from `df2`, matching the cases in `df1`. Retains ALL cases from left data frame `df1`, and adds `NA` for variables from `df2` that have no match.

:::::::: columns
:::::: {.column width="50%"}
::::: columns
::: {.column width="40%"}
```{r eval = F}
df1
```

```{r echo = F}
kable(df1) %>%
  kable_styling(font_size = 25)
```
:::

::: {.column width="40%"}
```{r eval = F}
df2
```

```{r echo = F}
kable(df2)%>%
  kable_styling(font_size = 25)
```
:::
:::::

```{r eval = F}
left_join(df1, df2, by = "ID")
```

```{r echo = F}
left_join(df1, df2, by = "ID") |>
  kable()%>%
  kable_styling(font_size = 25)
```
::::::

::: {.column width="50%"}
![Think of left data frame as fixed.](figs/08-left-join.gif){width="438"}
:::
::::::::

Adds columns to `df1` from `df2`, matching the cases in `df2`. Retains ALL cases from right data frame `df2`, and adds `NA` for variables from `df1` that have no match.

## `full_join(df1, df2)`

Adds columns to `df1` from `df2`, *full*y combining the two data frames, matching when possible. Retains ALL cases from `df1` AND `df2`, and adds `NA`s as necesary.

:::::::: columns
:::::: {.column width="50%"}
::::: columns
::: {.column width="40%"}
```{r eval = F}
df1
```

```{r echo = F}

  kable_styling(font_size = 25)
```
:::

::: {.column width="40%"}
```{r eval = F}
df2
```

```{r echo = F}
kable(df2)%>%
  kable_styling(font_size = 25)
```
:::
:::::

```{r eval = F}

```

```{r echo = F}

## `inner_join(df1, df2)`

Adds columns to `df1` from `df2`, retaining only cases that exist in both `df1` AND `df2`.

:::::::: columns
:::::: {.column width="50%"}
::::: columns

```

::: {.column width="40%"}
```{r eval = F}

```

```{r echo = F}
kable(df2)%>%
  kable_styling(font_size = 25)
```
:::
:::::

```{r eval = F}

```

## Comprehension check

::: discuss
1.  In which of the joins are `NA`s possibly introduced? In which of the joins are `NA`s never going to be introduced?
2.  If we have some `df1` and `df2`, in what scenario will the result of the four joins be the same? (i.e. what has to be true about `df1` and `df2`?)
3.  What do you think we call these "mutating" joins? *Think about where we've seen that verb before!*
:::

-   Note: it's possible to join on more than one variable!

## Example

```{r echo = F}
library(readr)
fish_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/midd-stat201-spring2025/midd-stat201-spring2025.github.io/refs/heads/main/data/fisheries.csv"
countries_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/math118-fall2022/website/refs/heads/master/docs/slides/lec-slides/data/continents.csv"
fish <- read_csv(fish_url)
continents <- read_csv(countries_url) |>
  rename("Country" = "country")
```

:::::::: columns
::::: {.column width="50%"}
We have data on fishery harvests (in tons) by countries from 2016, stored in data frame `fish`:

::: discuss
What does this code do?
:::

```{r eval = F}
fish |>
    slice(1:8)
```

::: fragment
```{r echo = F}
fish |>
  slice(1:8) |>
  kable() |>
  kable_styling(font_size = 20)
```
:::
:::::

:::: {.column width="50%"}
::: fragment
Suppose I would like to explore the data on a continent level. We have another data frame called `continent` that looks like this:

```{r eval = F}
continents |>
  slice(1:8)
```

```{r echo = F}
continents |>

  kable() |>
  kable_styling(font_size = 20)
```
:::
::::

## Example (cont.)

:::::: columns
::: {.column width="\"50%"}
Question 1:

```{r eval = F}
#| code-line-numbers: "1|2"

          by = c("country" = "Country")) |>
  slice(1:8)
```

```{r echo = F}

```

-   Notice the `NA`
:::

:::: {.column width="\"50%"}
::: fragment
Question 2:

```{r eval = F}
inner_join(fish, continents, 
           by = c("country" = "Country")) |>
  slice(1:8)
```

```{r echo = F}
inner_join(fish, continents, by = c("country" = "Country")) |>
  slice(1:8) |>
  kable() |>

```
:::
::::
::::::

-   Notice we don't have two copies of same `country`/`Country` variable!

## Piping into `xxx_join()`

::: discuss
In the following line of code, when would an `NA` be introduced? (Answer forthcoming.)
:::

```{r eval = F}
right_join(fish, continents, by = c("country" = "Country"))
```

-   Remember in data wrangling, we pipe from a previous line of code directly into another

-   We can pipe directly into the join functions! The following achieves the same as above:

::: fragment
```{r eval = F}
fish |>
  right_join(continents, by = c("country" = "Country"))
```
:::

## Answer to previous question

`NA`s would be introduced if there is a country in `continents` that does not appear in `fish`. See the last 50-ish cases:

```{r echo = F}
shrink_DT <- function(tbl, scale = 0.6) {
  htmltools::tags$div(
    style = paste0("transform: scale(", scale, "); transform-origin: top left;"),
    tbl
  )
}
shrink_DT(fish |>
  right_join(continents, by = c("country" = "Country")) |>
  DT::datatable())
```
